analysis:
This batch is documentation and changelog only: changelog.d/provider-prompt-token-reuse.md (new), docs/architecture/components/provider.md (lines 75-88, date bump) and docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~1030-1048). No executable code is supplied, so I cannot verify the described behavior.

The docs describe three behavior changes whose implementation (PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites, ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift, awaitReleasedLoads) is outside the supplied evidence:
1. Per-scope reuse of token IDs for chat-template pieces. This is relevant to T-041 and A-001. Docs state reuse never crosses a cache scope and is gated by the prefix-cache scope (the coordinator-authored cacheSalt). The security question is whether the token cache is keyed by the authenticated scope. If it is not, it adds a cross-tenant timing channel beyond the SEC-035 accepted risk, and the token cache would hold plaintext-derived token IDs in memory. Also check that DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 or a missing scope bypasses the cache, that its memory is bounded, and that eviction on scope change works.
2. Equivalent linear-time rewrites of the Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS templates. These are guarded by load-time and sampled background comparisons. Check that a mismatch fails closed to the served template and that sampled comparisons do not log prompt content (A-001, TB-007).
3. Cold-load release of the work consumer. This is relevant to TB-002 and T-053. A cancel is deferred until admission returns, and later requests, cancels and attestation challenges proceed during the load. Verify that an App Attest grant or connection invalidation arriving mid-load is honored before the waiting request begins inference. Check that ordering of the coordinator's inference/cancel pairs cannot let a cancelled or stale-connection request run. Also check capacity-check races (T-010 and availability).

The docs themselves do not weaken a control, so I report no finding. Because the unseen code carries cache-scope isolation and authorization-ordering implications, I recommend deeper review of those source files.
